# wisp

> Open-source launcher that runs AI coding agents (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, opencode, Cursor CLI, Antigravity CLI, Grok Build) in the background and hands back a 30-second animated presentation instead of a 4,000-line transcript.

- Website: https://trywisp.dev/
- GitHub: https://github.com/M0xoo/wisp
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/wisp-agents
- License: MIT
- Requirements: Node.js >= 20 and at least one supported coding agent CLI installed and signed in.

## Quick start

```sh
npx wisp-agents
npx wisp-agents "fix the flaky auth test"
npx wisp-agents --browser
```

Global install:

```sh
npm install -g wisp-agents
wisp "fix the flaky auth test"
wisp --mode plan "audit dependencies"
```

## Supported agent harnesses

- **Claude Code** (`claude`)
- **OpenAI Codex** (`codex`)
- **opencode** (`opencode`)
- **Cursor CLI** (`cursor-agent`)
- **Antigravity CLI** (`agy`)
- **Grok Build** (`grok`)

## Key features

- **Queue, not a chat log**: Sessions are grouped into `Needs you`, `Working` (live one-line status), and `Done`.
- **21 presentation blocks**: Agents finish with structured JSON blocks (`hero`, `diff`, `tests`, `stats`, `steps`, `files`, `commits`, `graph`, `tree`, `code`, `compare`, `flow`, `chart`, `terminal`, `checklist`, `callout`, `image`, `question`, `actions`, `markdown`, `next`).
- **Real diffs**: Captured directly from the agent's own file-edit tool calls.
- **Mid-run questions (`ask_user`)**: Every agent gets an `ask_user` MCP tool so it can ask clarifying questions mid-run; user answers resume the running session.
- **Terminal takeover**: Press `T` to open the session in Terminal, iTerm, Ghostty, Warp, cmux, kitty, WezTerm, or Windows Terminal with the agent's native `--resume` command.
- **Permission modes**: `Plan` (read-only), `Edits` (auto-accept file edits), `Full auto` (unattended commands, edits, and tests).
- **Learns as you go**: After a session goes quiet, a background retro records your preferences and the agent's lessons, globally and per project; later runs get them in their prompt. Review and edit them in the Memory view.
- **Rerun & updates**: Rerun any task with another harness/model (`⇧R`); an in-app Update button installs new `wisp-agents` releases.
- **Worktree per task & Ship it**: Each task runs in its own git worktree and branch; one click (`S`) commits, pushes and opens the PR, then follows CI and reviews; **Merge** squash-merges.
- **Subagents**: Give the lead agent a team on other harnesses (e.g. Claude Code delegating to Codex ×3) through a `delegate` tool.
- **Checkpoints & rollback**: Every turn is snapshotted; restore to before any turn or revert a single file.
- **Machines**: Run agents on your other computers over SSH (hosts found in `~/.ssh/config`, Tailscale and `known_hosts`); **Run on** sends one prompt to this computer and several machines in parallel, as one task with a row per machine.
- **Compare, recipes, triggers**: Run one task on two harnesses side by side; saved prompts with `{params}`; triggers on a schedule, failed CI or labelled issues.
- **Usage & phone**: Spend and success rate per project and model; questions and finished tasks on ntfy or Telegram.
- **Zero runtime dependencies**: The server uses Node.js built-ins only and stores plain JSON state in `~/.wisp`.

## Integrations & programmatic surfaces

- **MCP server**: `wisp mcp` (stdio MCP server exposing `wisp_launch`, `wisp_wait`, `wisp_get`, `wisp_reply`, `wisp_list`, `wisp_stop`, `wisp_agents`).
- **Agent skill**: `wisp skill install --agent all`
- **Scripting CLI**: `wisp "…" --json`, `wisp ls`, `wisp show <id>`, `wisp wait <id>`, `wisp reply <id> "…"`, `wisp stop <id>`
- **JavaScript SDK**: `import { WispClient } from 'wisp-agents'`
- **HTTP + SSE API**: `GET /api/openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.1), `POST /api/sessions`, `GET /api/events`
- **Webhooks**: `PATCH /api/config` with `session.waiting` and `session.finished` events.
